canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0006629
canonical_go_metadata.value: The chemical reactions and pathways involving lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent. Includes fatty acids; neutral fats, other fatty-acid esters, and soaps; long-chain (fatty) alcohols and waxes; sphingoids and other long-chain bases; glycolipids, phospholipids and sphingolipids; and carotenes, polyprenols, sterols, terpenes and other isoprenoids.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0006893
canonical_go_metadata.value: The directed movement of substances from the Golgi to the plasma membrane in transport vesicles that move from the trans-Golgi network to the plasma membrane. Golgi to plasma membrane transport precedes exocytosis.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0006893
canonical_go_metadata.value: Golgi to plasma membrane vesicle-mediated transport

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0008152
canonical_go_metadata.value: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism transforms chemical substances. This includes including anabolism (biosynthetic process) and catabolism (catabolic process). Metabolic processes includes the transformation of small molecules, as well  macromolecular processes such as DNA repair and replication, protein synthesis and degradation.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0008152
canonical_go_metadata.value: Note that metabolic processes do not include single functions or processes such as protein-protein interactions, protein-nucleic acids, nor receptor-ligand interactions.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0009058
canonical_go_metadata.value: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism synthesizes chemical substances. This typically represents the energy-requiring part of metabolism in which simpler substances are transformed into more complex ones.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0016020
canonical_go_metadata.value: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0030133
canonical_go_metadata.value: Any of the vesicles of the constitutive secretory pathway, which carry cargo from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, between Golgi cisternae, from the Golgi to the ER (retrograde transport) or to destinations within or outside the cell.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0030133
canonical_go_metadata.value: Note that the term 'secretory vesicle' is sometimes used in this sense, but can also mean 'secretory granule ; GO:0030141'.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0031012
canonical_go_metadata.value: A structure lying external to one or more cells, which provides structural support, biochemical or biomechanical cues for cells or tissues.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0055085
canonical_go_metadata.value: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0055085
canonical_go_metadata.value: Transmembrane transport is the transport of a solute across a lipid bilayer. Note that transport through the nuclear pore complex is not transmembrane because the nuclear membrane is a double membrane and is not traversed. For transport through the nuclear pore, consider instead the term 'nucleocytoplasmic transport ; GO:0006913' and its children. Note also that this term is not intended for use in annotating lateral movement within membranes.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0071705
canonical_go_metadata.value: The directed movement of nitrogen-containing compounds into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0016192
canonical_go_metadata.value: A cellular transport process in which transported substances are moved in membrane-bounded vesicles; transported substances are enclosed in the vesicle lumen or located in the vesicle membrane. The process begins with a step that directs a substance to the forming vesicle, and includes vesicle budding and coating. Vesicles are then targeted to, and fuse with, an acceptor membrane.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0048193
canonical_go_metadata.value: The directed movement of substances into, out of or within the Golgi apparatus, mediated by vesicles.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0005798
canonical_go_metadata.value: Any vesicle associated with the Golgi complex and involved in mediating transport within the Golgi or between the Golgi and other parts of the cell.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0005798
canonical_go_metadata.value: Note that this definition includes vesicles that are transiently associated with the Golgi.

canonical_go_metadata.subject: GO:0005737
canonical_go_metadata.value: The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.
